reasoning: Re-opened BZONE.MAC:3067-3113 (R.40$/R.50$) and enemies.ts:216-647. The load-bearing risk was ATRACT polarity: if bit7-set meant attract mode, R.50$ (the 50% coin) would run only in the demo. Grepped every ATRACT branch — :480 `BIT ATRACT / BMI 16$` skips the COPYRIGHT draw when in-game, :2614/:4041 comment 'IF IN GAME' with `BMI` to the in-game path, :667 `STA ATRACT` stores A=0 'SET TO ATTRACT'. So bit7 SET = IN GAME. At :3067 `R.40$: BIT ATRACT / BPL R.RAND` therefore sends attract→random-wander and falls through to R.50$ during real gameplay. Decoding R.50$: (a) FTIMER==$FF ⇒ R.ATCK; (b) `LDA PRAND / LSR / BCC R.ATCK` — LSR shifts bit0 into carry, BCC taken when bit0==0, so a fair 50% of decisions branch to attack BEFORE any score logic; (c) HITS+1 set ⇒ attack; (d) score-sign SBC HITS+2 ⇒ equal=evade / player-behind=random / player-ahead=attack. Attack floor is exactly 50%, rising as the player leads — attack-DOMINANT. Only 'charge' re-locks the live bearing and lines up a shot (:644-647); flank strafes ±90° and its barrel drifts off (no fire), so charge is the sole ROM-'attack' analog and it is a deliberate 0.3 minority. Genuine divergence: clone pursues ~0.3 of re-picks (non-repeating) where the ROM attacks ≥0.5. (An un-aligned charge auto-extends at :622-623, so real-world attack share exceeds the raw 0.3, but the per-decision odds and no-repeat rule are the structural divergence and stand.) Decode is accurate; no numeric correction.

Re-opened FIREIT BZONE.MAC:3137-3146 and enemies.ts:243-663. `.RADIX 16` region. FIREIT: `JSR TRACK` (bearing to player in A), `SEC / SBC TANGLE+2` (error = bearing − barrel; TANGLE+2 is the robot's own facing), abs via `BPL 10$` else `CLC / EOR I,0FF / ADC I,2`, then `10$: CMP I,2 / BCS 50$` — no-fire when the value ≥ 2. Fire requires error < 2 angle-units. At 360/256 = 1.40625°/unit that is a <2.81° ceiling; because the compare is on an integer byte the effective pass band is error 0-1 unit ≈ ≤1.41° (the negative-side abs idiom EOR $FF/ADC I,2 = |err|+1 makes that side even tighter, so the ROM window is if anything narrower than the finding states). Clone fires when |errPlayer| ≤ FIRE_CONE = 0.12 rad = 6.875° (enemies.ts:251, applied :661), and :661 ADDS `(1−aggro)*MILD_FIRE_EXTRA` (0.55 rad) for a low-aggro tank — wider still. 6.875/2.8125 = 2.44× the ROM ceiling, ~4.9× the effective ~1.41°. Divergence real and correctly signed (clone wider). The 'must retune with E-002/E-011' coupling is corroborated by the clone's own comment (:243-249) openly admitting it tuned the cone UP 'so the slow-turning maneuvering tank still catches the player' — a self-declared compensation for the rarer attack disposition (E-002) and the sub-ROM sweep... except the sweep is tuned FASTER (E-011), so the fire-cone widening compensates chiefly for the rarer attack. Numbers accurate; no correction.

Re-opened ROBCHK window routine BZONE.MAC:3752-3772 + ROB1 :3788-3867 and enemies.ts:317-352. `.RADIX 16`. Decoded the mask build: from the player−enemy differential `LDA HITS / SBC HITS+2`, min window ($0F) when player behind/even (BCC/BEQ 10$), else cap at 7 (`CMP I,7 / BCC 8$`, else `LDA I,7`), then `LSR` (diff>>1) and a `SEC/ROL` loop shifting extra 1-bits into a base of $0F: yields $0F, $1F, $3F, $7F as the differential climbs 1→7. ROB1 forms offset = `PRAND AND mask`, sign-flipped by an $INTCT bit (entropy sub, already STRUCTURAL C-007), `ADC TANGLE`, and the unit vector is added to the player position TPOSX/TPOSY (:3855-3867). $0F = 15 units = ±21.1°; $7F = 127 units = ±178.6°. So the spawn arc is score-SCALED ±21°→±178°, graduated, centred on the facing. Clone: SPAWN_FORWARD_ARC = Math.PI (enemies.ts:317), `dir = player.heading + (nextFloat−0.5)*π` (:349) = a FIXED ±90° off player.heading, no coupling to the aggression differential difficulty.ts already computes. Wider than the ROM's mild case, narrower than its full-aggro case, constant throughout — exactly the divergence claimed. (Clone does center on player.heading, matching the ROM center; the divergence is solely the fixed-vs-scaled arc width, which stands regardless of whether TANGLE is the player's or the new tank's angle.) Confirmed; no correction.

This is the operand the prompt flagged as a likely false-finding source; it survives. Re-opened TR7CHK BZONE.MAC:3704-3708 and the NOR2D3 lifecycle. TR7CHK: `CLC / LDA NOR2D3 / BMI 10$` (the $80-$FF sentinel band stays carry-clear = regular tank) `/ CMP I,5` (carry set ⇔ NOR2D3 ≥ 5) with comment 'CLEAR CARRY FOR TANK', so carry-set = TR7 super. NOR2D3 semantics verified three ways: `.BLKB 1 ;# OF R2D3'S -1 THIS GAME` (:301), game-start `LDA I,-1 / STA NOR2D3` (:1175-1176), and `R2D3CK: INC NOR2D3 ;C THIS WILL SET NOR2D3 TO 0 FOR FIRST` (:3773). So NOR2D3 = (missiles spawned) − 1, and NOR2D3 ≥ 5 first holds when missiles = 6 → super tank appears after the 6th missile. Clone: chooseKind (enemies.ts:366-370) returns super when `missilesLaunched >= SUPER_TANK_AFTER_MISSILES` (=5); missilesLaunched starts at 0 (:377/:491) and increments AFTER the kind decision (:501-502), so it equals the count launched so far → super at the 5th missile. The clone treats its from-0 counter as if it were NOR2D3, but NOR2D3 is from −1 (missiles−1); they differ by exactly 1, so the clone's super tank arrives one missile-wave early. Clean off-by-one, CMP I,5 correctly decoded; the finding is right. Fix would be `>= 6` (or seed the counter at −1). No numeric correction to the finding.

Re-opened ITANGL BZONE.MAC:2826-2833, the ROBOT pivot path :2986-3008, and enemies.ts:201-202 + movement.ts:39-51. `.RADIX 16`. ITANGL: `LDA I,80 / CLC / ADC LANGLE ... ADC TANGLE` adds $0080 to the 16-bit angle TANGLE:LANGLE where TANGLE (high byte) is the 256-unit circle position — $0080/$10000 = 0.5 unit = 0.703°/call. ROBOT's big-turn (pivot) branch calls ITANGL twice for a regular tank (:2988-2991) and, when `JSR TR7CHK / BCS` says super, two more (:2995-2998) = 4 total → 1 unit/frame regular, 2 units/frame super = 1.406°/2.813° per frame. At the ground-truth 15.625 Hz game frame: 1.40625°×15.625 = 21.97°/s regular, 43.95°/s super. Clone: MAX_TURN_RATE = (2π/512)×2×60 = 84.375°/s (verified via movement.ts:39/45/51); TANK_TURN_RATE = 0.4× = 33.75°/s, SUPER = 0.7× = 59.06°/s. Ratios 33.75/21.97 = 1.54× and 59.06/43.95 = 1.34× — matching the finding's '~1.5× and ~1.3×'. Knowing divergence (clone comment :192-199 cites 'the ROM's raw ~22°/s (super ~44°/s)' and states it is tuned UP). The clone's own timebase is 60 Hz (FRAMES_PER_SEC=60), but the comparison is in absolute °/s so it is frame-rate-independent and valid. Arithmetic accurate; no correction.

Re-opened FIREIT's restraint ladder BZONE.MAC:3120-3136 and the clone fire gate enemies.ts:656-663. `.RADIX 16`. After the $20 fire-grace (E-005), FIREIT at :3124 `CMP I,0FF / BEQ 5$` lets FTIMER==$FF (full aggression, ~16 s) skip all restraints; :3126 `LDA HITS+1 / BNE 5$` lets a high-score player skip them; :3128 `LDA HITS / LSR / BNE 5$` lets a non-rookie player skip them. Only for a rookie player before full aggression does control reach :3131 `LDA PTURN / CMP I,20 / BCS 2$` (not-in-view ⇒ no fire) and :3134 `LDA TDIST / CMP I,24 / BCS 50$` (TDIST ≥ $24 ⇒ too far ⇒ no fire). So the ROM genuinely withholds fire at long range in the early/rookie band. Clone fire gate (:656-663) tests only shell-availability, playerHit, reload, the 2 s SPAWN_FIRE_GRACE, and barrel alignment (:661) — NO range term; a freshly-spawned clone tank fires the instant it lines up at any distance (and :661's MILD_FIRE_EXTRA actually makes an early tank MORE lethal, the opposite of the ROM's mild restraint). Divergence real. $24 is an undecoded TDIST distance byte whose world-unit scale can't be pinned here — the finding already flags this and rests the verdict on the RESTRAINT's absence, not the exact range, so it is correctly hedged. Confirmed; no correction.
